ingredients.item: condensed milk or sugar — the grill-hall sweetness signature
/2 cucumber , small-diced, salted 10 minutes and squeezed

instructions.heading: Step 1
instructions.action: The dressing whisked smooth first — mayo, condensed milk, vinegar, salt — tasting distinctly sweeter than seems right at room temperature. It is: cold suppresses sweetness, and the chill will bring it to target.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: the dressing tastes sweet-tangy, pourable, just shy of a sauce — it will be swallowed by the pasta, so run it loose.

instructions.heading: Step 2
instructions.action: The drained, cooled, still-damp pasta and the dressing tossed while the pasta is cool but not fridge-cold (the dressing coats evenly at this temperature; fridge-cold pasta repels mayo), then the cucumber, carrot, egg, and scallion folded through.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: every noodle glossed, the mix-ins distributed, the bowl holding together without a puddle at the bottom. If it pools, the cucumber's squeeze was skipped.

instructions.heading: Step 3
instructions.action: Chill 30 minutes minimum, taste, and adjust — cold macaroni salad always needs one more grain of salt and a few drops of vinegar at the finish.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: the eating test between bites of bulgogi (#M01): cold, sweet, soft-with-crunch, mild — the palate's reset button, which is the entire reason the grill halls serve it and the reason this bowl rides alongside the richest plates.

storageNotes: Keeps 2 days refrigerated; refresh at serving with a spoon of mayo and a drop of vinegar — the bowl revives well.
Variations: the potato sibling (#B21); finely diced ham for the lunchbox build; a pinch of gochugaru over the top for the table that wants even this bowl to carry a little heat.
